title: TE Caleb Lohner, minicamp participants meet media
text: How far have you come along? I think >> I've come a long way, you know, and just at the end of the day want to be here for the team. Um, want to do what I can to help win and prepare the right way, play the right way, and I think this is a great organization to do it. So, >> how about uh you saying that you played some outside linebacker on scout team last year? You were a two-way player. >> What did you get out of that? >> I had to help VJ a couple times with certain, you know, personnel stuff. There were a couple injuries, but had a good time doing it. I think, you know, it's uh it's practice, but the end of the day, I think I'm going to stick with tight end. >> Can you put in perspective or quantify how much more comfortable you are a year later compared to where you were at this rookie camp after being here for a year? >> Yeah, I just think, you know, being in the system, being around the vets, seeing kind of how things go has helped me a lot. um kind of having a confidence and comfortability and how things operate, you know, not being crazy and, you know, kind of confused with how the playbook is, stuff like that. And so feel a lot more comfortable. I'm super grateful to be with an organization and coaches that believe in me and I'm excited to do what I can to help this team win. >> What did you do in the offseason just to improve your game? >> Um lots of training, um film work, body work, physical stuff, mental stuff, all the above. How often do you pick up a basketball and any of your teammates try to challenge you at a one-on-one game at any point? >> Oh, have they? Um, they probably will down the line, but I'm pretty confident. >> They drafted a couple of tight ends. What was your reaction to that? >> Um, I don't have a reaction. Whoever's in our room, you know, we all want to make each other better. We all want to push each other. And so, um, that's, you know, that's their role upstairs. Our role is just to come out every day, play, prepare, and do what we can to help the team. >> Some basketball players making the transition to football realize the contact is much different than getting a rebound. >> It's different. >> Can you explain how, you know, you made that transition? >> Yeah, I mean, it just takes getting used to, right? Um, and I think this has been such a great team to work on that because I think we have an exceptional defensive line, edge players, and so, um, just continue to working on that. Um, I think I've come a long way when it comes to physicality, but yeah, it it's a lot different >> with the u the, you know, you're on a try out basis here. You had a try out with the Kansas City Chiefs. What are you hoping to get out of all this? >> Yeah, you never know when it's going to be your last time. So, just having fun, like I said, playing quarterback again. Um, I feel like I can play in this league and just kind of hoping for an opportunity. Um, so it's really cool to come in here with an awesome organization like this. I looked up to Drew Brees when I was growing up and and watched so much Saints film back in the day. Um, so it's just cool to kind of come in here and learn from coach Payton, learn from coach Webb, coach Kilgore, and just go out there and try to play football again. >> Drew Brees, was that because of size by any chance? >> Size? I feel like I played similar to him for sure. Uh, shorter side, but accurate, make the right decisions, and obviously he was the best at that. Um, so it was cool to watch him all going up. >> EJ, what's it like going from one, you know, like one system one weekend to another the next weekend and trying, you know, trying to sort of pick that up on the fly? >> Yeah. Um, it can be difficult. just you hear one word and it means this, then you hear the same word and it means something else. But it's football. Uh, everyone moves around in this league. I grew up learning systems uh with my dad all the time. So, it's not too challenging. Just got to make sure you put in the time and study uh so you can come prepared and make these coaches know that you are smart enough to play this position. >> What's the best advice you got from dad with this stuff? >> Um, I mean, yeah, just go out there and have fun is his main thing. Um, obviously like I said, there's expectations involved and his everyone's journey is different, especially his journey and he's told me that where it doesn't always look the best at every moment, but just go out there and when you have the chance, go out there and sling it and play confident. Once you start second guessing yourself, that's when you're in trouble. Just go out there, trust your eyes, believe in yourself, and go play. Have fun playing quarterback. >> I wouldn't say unbelievable, but almost unbelievable. Uh, just knowing I just felt like, man, you know, when you start 39 straight games with no injuries, two-time captain, do what I did. you know, feel like I was going to get dropped, but you know, I know God had a greater plan for me. So, wasn't much panic there. When you have a shakable uh faith, you have great poise, man. That type of thing don't uh shake you up too much. So, you know, just uh I'm exactly where I belong, exactly where I am on God's plan. So, you know, >> you didn't get too down about it. >> I was never down about it, man. You know, we have a plan for everything. Getting drafted, not getting drafted. Me and my mom and agent had a plan. So, uh you know, we had to go to plan B, but ain't nothing wrong with that. >> What was your interaction with the Broncos? I mean, how much did you talk to them before the draft? And then at what point did you kind of commit to them if you didn't get drafted? Yeah, I knew they liked me a lot and I liked them a lot. I know obviously they were a team that was on the brink of going to the Super Bowl and winning the Super Bowl to be honest with you. Uh, what really enticed me about the Broncos was their pass rush for sure. It's kind of same thing when I went to&m too. You know, when I went to&M I was the last guy offered, the lowest ranked guy in my class. You know what I'm saying? Nobody really expected much from me. Uh, and so like that's why I committed&M because they had Walter Nolan, Shamar Stewart, Turner, LT Overton, McKinley Jackson. I can go acknowledge him on the defensive line I played in front of. So a great defensive line definitely helps me play my game a whole lot better. You think you're a guy I mean they've had undrafted free agents make the team regularly here. I mean that's obviously your goal. What do you think your >> Yeah, I'm just a guy that's playing football right now. Just doing my job, learning uh you know the scope of the Denver Broncos organization.

title: TE Dallen Bentley on rookie minicamp: ‘I love being out here’
text: What have What have these past few weeks been like from being drafted to now the transition of being here? Yeah, I mean, it's been pretty great. You know, it's a really fast process. You know, things happen quickly then next thing you know, you're out here and you you got the playbook and you're studying as much as you can. You know, I love it all. It's great. What What was the first day like out there catching passes and having Sean Payton coach you? Super fun, you know. I love being out here. Love to start playing some football again and yeah, I'm just taking in every opportunity. The journey you had from going to Snow and then to Utah, can you just take us through that? What that was like? Obviously, Bulls did the Yeah. there, so Yeah. Yeah, me and Bulls, yeah. Same pathway there. We actually both served a mission here as well, so it's a full circle, which is pretty sweet and yeah, you know, Snow College just got to take every opportunity you can to get better and that's something I might take a lot of pride in, you know, just coming to work every single day and finding those little things I can improve on and you know, it'll pay off eventually. But most guys when they get here, they're not familiar with the area, but did you did your mission like what? Down the street basically? Yeah, I did. I lived in a couple different places. Um, just right around here, so really familiar. It's pretty sweet. What How just as you have sort of grown as a football player, I mean, where where did you along the way did you realize that sort of blocking, you know, came natural to you or that that could be a strong point in in your game? >> [clears throat] >> Uh, I mean I've got the body for it, you know, so that's there and then it always just came down to working on my technique and then, you know, just kind of piece by piece it it all kind of just fit in, so kind of just came slowly, I guess I'd say. It's the third straight year they've brought in a Utah rookie tight end. There was Yassmin 2 years ago. Loa is still here, obviously. You talked to those guys a little bit about what it's [snorts] like and they give you some info and all that or Yeah, yeah, definitely. You know, Thomas is my guy. Caleb is my guy, so yeah. Um, I'm I'm glad I get to be here with Caleb and they're super awesome. They can they help me out in any way that any questions I have, they're always super friendly and obviously willing to help out. So, it's pretty great.

title: TE Justin Joly: ‘It’s amazing to be a Denver Bronco’
text: The coaches they just put me in great positions, you know, between coach King and coach Wade, you know, they're just telling me what to do and just putting me there. So, and that's what all the tight ends do between me, Dalton, uh Stoner, and Miguel. So, they just put us in great positions, honestly. What's your first impression of Davis? Just, you know, obviously new play caller here, but just in 2 days, you know, working with him and and going through it. What have you thought about him so far? Great vibe and he wants to win and I love it. I love I want to win, too. What's like the main thing you got to learn all this is being thrown at you right away? What are some of the things that you know been like all the information coming at you? Just honestly, whatever the coaches tell you tell you what to do. Just like go out there, do this route, make sure you do it correctly, you know. Go watch film, come back. If I did something wrong, the coach is going to let me know. I'm going to try to come back and be better next time. What have these past 2 weeks been like with getting drafted and then having this transition and now getting here? Honestly, it was wonderful. You know, I'm blessed. I'm It's amazing to be a Denver Bronco. I got a great support system within my family and within the staff itself. Like I I felt like I never left home. How has your life changed in the last 2 weeks now that you're in the NFL? Uh just straight ball. That's it. Just straight ball. Any Any reason for the 88 jersey? This is just what they gave me and I'm I'm grateful for it. So, let's do it. What What's been your impression of a guy who was here last year, but also a former basketball player, Caleb Lonner? Veteran Sean Payton was just singing his praises a little bit. Like, what have you seen from him just the past couple days? Super uber athletic. Yeah. No, he he could jump out the sky. Fast, quick twitch, you know, and it's great, you know, all the tight ends we get to learn from him just asking as many questions as possible, you know. He's an older guy, so he helps us out, too. So, it's wonderful. Like, I'm happy to have Caleb in the room. What did you learn from the blocking drills the last 2 days? Uh coach King, just working on techniques and just getting better, you know, not only with hand work, but foot work as well. Obviously, you had just a lot of red zone production last year. I think seven touchdowns in six games. How do you see be you know, kind of transitioning to the NFL where you know, maybe you're not a 6-6, 6-7 guy, but the vertical, the athleticism. Like, how do you kind of see yourself being able to make an impact? >> Honestly, it's where the coaches want to put me. So, it's like, if you want to put me in the backfield, if you want to put me anywhere on the field, I'll do it. Even if they want me to play defense, I'm just let me know, I got you guys. You chatted with Bo yet? Not yet. Okay. What are you looking forward to chatting with him about? Uh just be like, "Hey, if you ever need someone, um I'm your guy."
